The Oba of Lagos, Rilwan Akiolu, has urged politicians to shun violence and allow their records and past performance to speak for them, warning that Nigerians do not want political rancour and bloodshed. Akiolu said candidates should focus on presenting their programmes and achievements to Nigerians rather than resorting to hostility, adding that the country needed cooperation, patience and peaceful political engagement. The monarch spoke after the installation of the new Kakawa of Lagos, High Chief Jamiu Kakawa, and Eletu of Iwashe, High Chief Teslim Oluwatosin, at his palace in Iduganran, Lagos Island, on Tuesday. He said, “My pleading to all of us in this country is we should give peace a chance. See the programmes of all the aspirants, see what they have done, and pray for them and support them and all will be well with us.” The traditional ruler, who urged politicians to be guided by their records rather than political hostility, said their past conduct and performance should determine how Nigerians assessed them. In life, a man doesn’t get to position and you don’t know how he has behaved,” he said. Akiolu, who noted that Lagosians were opposed to violence and rancour, urged those with resources to support the less privileged rather than accumulate excessive wealth. “Lagosians don’t want rancour, violence. The one that has should give the one that does not have. Why amass so much riches?” he asked. Delta killings: Police invite Omo-Agege, LG chairman, five others 2027: SDP demands equal police protection for all parties Don’t turn 2027 elections into battlefield, INEC chairman warns politicians His appeal comes amid reported attacks and disruptions involving political activities in parts of the country, including the killing of supporters during a campaign visit by former Deputy President of the Senate, Ovie Omo-Agege, in Delta State, and the recent disruption of a meeting of the Nigeria Democratic Congress in Lagos. Speaking further, the monarch appealed to Nigerians to give President Bola Tinubu more time to address the country’s challenges, saying the incumbent’s performance should be considered in assessing his administration. “As far as I am concerned, the performance of the incumbent president speaks a lot for him. We have experienced many things around this area. With God on our side, and the cooperation of our people, all went well,” he said. He added, “My special appeal to all Nigerians is to give more time to the incumbent president on this assignment and with the support and prayers of all of us, all will be well. We need patience.” Akiolu called for cooperation, prayers and closeness to God, expressing optimism that the country would overcome its challenges. “All we require in this country is cooperation, prayer and closeness to God,” he said. On state police, the monarch commended the new State Police Law but stressed that its success would depend on impartial enforcement and implementation. “Anybody can make a law but the application is what matters. If it is approached and enforced and implemented with the fear of God, everything will be in order,” he said.
